author: massicomar
title: Coin Combinations II
summary:
Consider a money system consisting of $n$ coins. Each coin has a positive integer value. Your task is to calculate the number of distinct ordered ways you can produce a money sum $x$ using the available coins.

For example, if the coins are $\{2,3,5\}$ and the desired sum is $9$, there are $3$ ways:

- $2+2+5$
- $3+3+3$
- $2+2+2+3$

Input

The first input line has two integers $n$ and $x$: the number of coins and the desired sum of money.

The second line has $n$ distinct integers $c_1,c_2,\dots,c_n$: the value of each coin.

Output

Print one integer: the number of ways modulo $10^9+7$.

constraints.text: n ≤ 100 coins, x ≤ 1e6, unordered ways, mod 1e9+7

explanation: Unordered ways: process coin types one at a time, so each multiset is built in a fixed order and counted once.
traps: Using sum-outer loops counts permutations instead (Coin Combinations I).

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[i][s] = number of ways to make s using only the first i coin types (rolled into dp[s])
dp[s] = number of ordered sequences summing to s
options.why: Counts 2+3 and 3+2 separately — that's Coin Combinations I.
Works only if you also force non-decreasing order; much bigger than needed.

options.text: dp[i][s] = 1 if coin i is used in sum s

extraLayers.explanation: Fixing the order in which coin types are considered makes each multiset appear exactly once.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: for each coin c (outer): for s in c..x: dp[s] += dp[s − c]
for s in 1..x (outer): for each coin c: dp[s] += dp[s − c]
for each coin c: for s from x down to c: dp[s] += dp[s − c]
options.why: Downward iteration allows each coin type at most once.

options.text: dp[s] = Σ dp[s − c] / (number of coins)
options.why: Dividing doesn't remove duplicate orderings correctly.

extraLayers.explanation: dp[i][s] = dp[i−1][s] + dp[i][s − c_i]: either never use coin i, or use it at least once more.

es.explanation: Formas sin orden: procesa los tipos de moneda de a uno, así cada multiconjunto se arma en un orden fijo y se cuenta una vez.
traps: Con las sumas en el loop de afuera se cuentan permutaciones (Coin Combinations I).

dp-state.explanation: Fijar el orden en que se consideran los tipos de moneda hace que cada multiconjunto aparezca exactamente una vez.

why.b: Cuenta 2+3 y 3+2 por separado: eso es Coin Combinations I.
why.c: Solo funciona si además fuerzas orden no decreciente; es mucho más grande de lo necesario.
why.d: No es una cantidad de combinaciones.

dp-transition.explanation: dp[i][s] = dp[i−1][s] + dp[i][s − c_i]: o nunca usas la moneda i, o la usas al menos una vez más.

why.b: Con las sumas afuera se cuentan los órdenes por separado.
why.c: Recorrer hacia abajo permite cada tipo de moneda a lo sumo una vez.
why.d: Dividir no saca bien los órdenes repetidos.
